changelog.text: Questions are easier to read, and answers are now hidden until you press Show answer (or use the Answers switch).
Removed citation text that duplicated the source chips.
Added source chips to topic sections and sourced worked questions; derived examples remain labelled in the audit.
Existing source citations now link to the original PDFs and textbook entries on the Sources page.
Added consistent syntax highlighting to C, Java and pseudocode snippets, with readable colors in light/dark themes and offline downloads.
Added a ▶ Revision videos button at the top of each unit: long GATE Wallah crash-course sessions for that unit plus two whole-OS one-shots.

Added ▶ Videos buttons: 80 checked YouTube videos (Neso Academy, Gate Smashers, Jenny's Lectures, GATE Wallah and others) linked to the sections and headings they explain, with solved-problem videos tagged and a note where a video differs from the notes.

Added questions from past RVCE SEE papers (2019–2023) and the 2024-25 CIE/SEE. Unit 1: fork() with || / && and fork vs vfork, plus an older-SEE question bank. Unit 2: six more worked SEE problems (LRTF, CPU utilization with I/O, three full scheduling sets, RR q=4 on the flagship set), and earlier examples now name the paper they came from. Unit 3: new past-paper question bank and four worked examples (single-request fits, EAT with TLB time, paging arithmetic, shared compiler).

Six new worked examples from the CIE-2 solved question bank: fractional-arrival FCFS/SJF/SRTF, priority with an SRTF tie-break, RMS vs EDF above the RMS bound, a combined SRTF/priority/RR set with response time, two GATE-style quick numericals, and two-semaphore lock ordering. Indexed in the question bank.

Removed duplicate copies of topics that only moved between units (old Unit 2 threads → Unit 1; old Unit 3 synchronization → Unit 2), each replaced by a link to its new home. Topics dropped from the new syllabus stay available behind View/Hide.

Unit 3 aligned to the faculty's new-syllabus main-memory slides: memory-hardware background, MFT/MVT, the slides' fixed-partition fit examples, 50-percent rule, modern and mobile swapping, static vs dynamic linking, TLB/PTLR details, and the structure of the page table (hierarchical, hashed, inverted).

Unit 2 synchronization (2.8–2.15) aligned to the faculty's updated slides: data-access vs control synchronization, disabling interrupts, bounded-waiting test_and_set algorithm, unbounded vs bounded buffers, first/second readers–writers problems, slide variable names (rw_mutex, read_count) and code.
Units 1–3 added for the CS235AT syllabus: OS foundations, processes and threads; CPU scheduling and synchronization; main memory management. Units 4–5 remain in progress.
